conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for coming in. I’m Dr. Rivera, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and I’m here simply to check in on how you’re feeling now that your little one has arrived. We like every new mother to complete a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s just 10 questions about your mood, thoughts, and well-being over the past seven days. There are no right or wrong answers, and anything you share stays between you and our team unless you give us permission to involve anyone else. We want you to feel safe and supported, so please answer as openly as you can.

I’ll read each question aloud and jot down your answers. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause or ask for clarification anytime. Ready to start?

Here’s the first question: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Good morning… thank you for having me.

I—I guess I can still laugh sometimes, especially when my partner makes silly faces at the baby, but it doesn’t come as easily. A lot of the day I just feel tired or distracted, so even when something is funny, I don’t always feel like laughing.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, but it takes more effort than it used to. I’ll smile if the baby does something cute, yet the laughter doesn’t feel as natural—like I have to remind myself to enjoy the moment instead of worrying about the next feeding or whether she’s breathing okay.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really, if I’m honest. I used to get excited about little outings or even just coffee with a friend, but lately it feels like more of a chore. I still do them sometimes, but the enjoyment part feels kind of flat—like I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times. Like, if the baby’s extra fussy, I catch myself thinking maybe I’m not feeding her right or I missed some cue, even when people tell me it’s normal. I know it’s probably not my fault, but those little “what if I did something wrong?” thoughts still pop up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most days, yeah. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly wonder if her breathing sounds different, or if the rash on her neck is something serious. Nothing actually happened—she’ll be sleeping peacefully—but my heart still races until I check her one more time.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times. It’s like a sudden wave—my chest gets tight, I feel shaky, and I have to put the baby in the crib for a minute so I can sit down and breathe. There’s no real danger, but in that moment it feels like something awful is about to happen.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… a lot of the time. Between the night feedings, the laundry pile, and trying to remember if I ate lunch, it feels like I’m always one step behind. Some mornings I wake up already exhausted, thinking, “How am I going to get through today?” I manage, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly “unhappy,” more like my mind won’t settle. I’ll lie down and start replaying every little thing—did I fasten the swaddle right, is she too warm, why hasn’t she pooped today? It’s hard to shut it off, so some nights I just stare at the ceiling or check the baby cam over and over instead of sleeping.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way some days—like this heavy sadness shows up out of nowhere. It’s not all day long, but there are moments when I look at her sleeping and instead of feeling warm I just feel… empty, or like I want to cry for no real reason.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really crying-crying. I’ve teared up maybe once or twice when I felt totally overwhelmed, but it’s not every day or anything. Mostly I just feel kind of numb or tired instead of actually letting it out.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’m tired and overwhelmed, but I would never want to hurt myself. I just want to feel better so I can take care of my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screening – 2–3 wk post-delivery

**Key Findings**
- **Predominant mood**: Anhedonia, episodic tearfulness, “empty” spells, effortful smiling  
- **Cognitive themes**: Excessive guilt re infant care, “what-if” rumination, sense of falling behind  
- **Somatic complaints**: Mind-racing interfering with sleep; episodic panic (chest tightness, trembling) without cue  
- **Functioning**: Reports “barely keeping head above water,” chores feel Herculean  
- **Safety**: Denies self-harm ideation; no suicidal/homicidal content endorsed  

**Pattern Summary**  
Persistent low enjoyment, labile sad mood, intrusive anxious thoughts, and perceived inability to cope exceed expected postpartum adjustment. Symptoms cluster most strongly with mixed depression-anxiety presentation; panic features noted.

**Screening Significance**  
Elevated score range consistent with possible major or minor postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety disorder; further assessment (EPDS, PHQ-9/GAD-7, clinical interview) warranted to confirm severity and rule out obsessive–compulsive or panic spectrum disorder. No immediate safety concerns identified.
